persona: 创始人·coding agent / 个人 agent CEO、CTO
q_zh: Meta 把 Wonder 放上 API，coding agent 的模型成本能降下来吗？
q_en: Meta put Muse Wonder on its API: will that bring down model costs for coding-agent startups?
lead_zh: coding agent、个人 agent 公司别指望 Meta 压低前沿模型成本（补记，写于 2026-11-13）：Wonder 10/12 上 API 标 $4/$20，比 Fable 5.1 低六成（自算），但与 Opus 5.5 同价；最强档 Full 只进 Muse Code 订阅，Meta 称与 Wonder 相当，11/13 仍无按量 API。
judgment_zh: 共识（10/12–10/15）是 Meta 追上前沿、挑战 Anthropic 和 OpenAI（Reuters 10/12 标题）；Meta 自称 API 会定在比 OpenAI、Anthropic 头部模型明显更低的位置（CNBC 10/12 转述 Alexandr Wang，二手），这句以 Fable 5.1 为参照成立、以 Opus 5.5 为参照不成立，Futurum 10/14（Nick Patience）已指出。日记的判断：前沿档上应用层只多了一个同价选项和一个自营对手 Muse Code，多一家前沿厂，不等于应用层多一份毛利。Meta 10/12 自称 Wonder 与 Full 性能相当，所以眼下伤害小；风险在结构：扎克伯格 10/21 称已在做 Wonder 之后的更大模型，如果它们也只进自家订阅，应用层能买到的和 Meta 自营产品用的就会拉开差距。同期降价的是在位者：11/9 Fable 5.2 比 5.1 低 20%（自算）；这是例行换代，还是对 Meta（10/12）或 Gemini 4 Argon（10/13 限时 $2/$10，二手）入场的回应，现有材料分不开。如果是后者，新入场者就是借在位者之手压低了成本；日记只说别把它写进毛利假设，不说它不会发生，也不说应用层毛利不会改善。「最强档留在自家订阅」是对意图的推断，另有算力、数据、Wonder 仍标 preview 等解释。
facts_zh: Meta 开发者博客 10/12：Wonder 每百万 token 输入 $4、输出 $20，Full 只通过 Muse Code 订阅提供（月费 $50、$200 两档），Meta 称两者性能相当；模型卡称 Full 是能力最强的变体。Anthropic 定价页 10/12 快照：Fable 5.1 为 $10/$50，Opus 5.5 为 $4/$20。Wonder 不是前沿最低价：VentureBeat 10/13 标题称 Google 给 Gemini 4 Argon 定了限时 $2/$10（二手）。Meta 跑分表（公司称）：AA 指数 Opus 5.5 为 58、Wonder 为 52，DeepSWE 1.1 Opus 5.5 为 74.2、Wonder 为 78.8；Meta 表中 14 项（不含 OSWorld binary）里 Opus 5.5 高 9 项、Wonder 高 5 项（自算），日记不对「同价谁更强」下结论。11/9 Meta 发布 Ember，20 万输入 token 以内每百万 token $0.10/$0.50，与 Haiku 5.5 起价相同，Meta 称最难的问题交给 Wonder；VentureBeat 11/10 标题称 Ember 每任务估算成本约为 Haiku 5.5 的 1/3（二手）。11/13 Meta 文档仍写 Full 在 Model API 上「Not available」，Wonder 标价未变、仍标 preview。
landing_zh: 对创业者：别把「接入最强模型」当护城河，把换模型成本压到底。最可能推翻本判断的路径，是扎克伯格 10/21 说的新小模型：以更高效率提供 Wonder 级能力，如果落地且更便宜，按证伪口 ③ 裁定。同一天他也说 Wonder 和正在训练的更强模型可服务 API 等高毛利业务（反向信号，按证伪口 ① 裁定），还预计一年后能用更小的模型、以一小部分成本提供 Wonder 级智能（公司称），这一点落在证伪窗口之外。对投资人：2027 年看 agent 融资，别把「多一家前沿厂」写进毛利假设，钱挪向换模型不伤体验、有自有数据或交易闭环的应用。
falsify_zh: 起算 2026-11-13，截至 2027-04-12（均按美西时间），共 150 天（自算）。只裁定正文两点：Meta 的最强档不进按量 API；Meta 不领头压低 Wonder 级能力的 API 标价。✗（任一发生即撤回主判断，作者改口）：① Muse Wonder Full，或 Meta 官方材料明确列为高于 muse-wonder-1.0 的更强型号（Full 的后继，或届时只进 Muse Code 订阅的更高档），在 Meta Model API 或 Meta 官方列出的任一第三方平台（如 Google Cloud、OpenRouter）出现公开的按 token 标价，并且可以按量调用；需要审批但有公开标价的也算；Full 或更高档只在 Muse Code 内改为按量计费（不在 Model API 或第三方平台上）不算 ①，记读数，因为应用层仍买不到；muse-wonder-1.0 本身及其同档改版不算 ①，归 ② 裁定。② muse-wonder-1.0 或同档的直接后继，在 Meta Model API 标准模式下的公开标价降到输入 ≤ $2.80 或输出 ≤ $14.00（每百万 token），即比 2026-11-13 的 $4/$20 低至少 30%（自算）；或者 Meta 为 Wonder 档开放 Contributor 模式，价格比标准价低至少 30%（11/13 时 Wonder 不提供 Contributor 模式）。③ 2026-11-13 之后，Meta 在 Model API 上推出任一新模型或现有系列的新版本（如 Spark、Ember 的新版本号），Meta 官方称其达到 Wonder 级（如扎克伯格 10/21 说的 Wonder-level，或同义表述），或 Meta 公布的同版本 AA 指数读数不低于 muse-wonder-1.0（10/12 表中为 52），且标准模式公开标价为输入 ≤ $2.80 或输出 ≤ $14.00（每百万 token）。不算 ✗、只记读数：限时促销、批量价、缓存价；达不到 Wonder 级的新小模型（如 11/9 的 Ember，Meta 称 AA 指数 36，最难的问题交给 Wonder）；没有公开标价的企业私下合同；第三方托管开放权重 Spark Open 的价格；跟降，即 Meta 降价或 ③ 的新模型上线前 30 天内，Anthropic Opus 档、OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 档或 Google Gemini 4 Argon 档（或各自的直接后继）的标准标价（不含限时价）先行降到同一水平或更低，这种情况 ②③ 不触发，记读数「跟降」。已验证：到 2027-04-12，Meta 文档与各平台都没有 Wonder Full 或届时最强档的按量标价，②③ 也没有发生。已验证只覆盖到 2027-04-12，不代表正文 6–18 个月的判断已成立；2027-10-21 前后按 ③ 的口径再记一次读数。在此之前一律记 ⏳。风险提示：Wonder 目前仍标 preview，转正式版时调价并不少见，按上面的规则照样裁定。
status_zh: ⏳ 进行中：ENTRY 147 为 2026-11-13 补记（事件日 2026-10-15），不计入事前命中；证伪口自 2026-11-13 起算、截至 2027-04-12，台账尚无对账或读数。
lead_en: Coding- and personal-agent firms shouldn't expect Meta to cut frontier costs (retrospective, written 2026-11-13): since 10/12 Wonder's API is $4/$20, 60% below Fable 5.1 (self-computed) but equal to Opus 5.5; top variant Full, on par with Wonder per Meta, is Muse Code-only, no metered API by 11/13.
judgment_en: Consensus (10/12–10/15) was that Meta had caught up with the frontier and was challenging Anthropic and OpenAI (Reuters headline, 10/12); Meta said its API would be priced clearly below the top models of OpenAI and Anthropic (Alexandr Wang as relayed by CNBC on 10/12, secondhand), which holds with Fable 5.1 as the reference and does not hold with Opus 5.5, as Futurum (Nick Patience) already pointed out on 10/14. The diary's call: at the frontier tier the app layer gained only a same-price option and a competitor run by its supplier, Muse Code; one more frontier lab does not mean one more slice of gross margin for the app layer. Meta said on 10/12 that Wonder and Full perform comparably, so the harm today is small; the risk is structural: Zuckerberg said on 10/21 that Meta is already building bigger models after Wonder, and if those also stay in its own subscription, a gap will open between what the app layer can buy and what Meta's own products use. The price cut in the period came from an incumbent: on 11/9 Fable 5.2 listed 20% below 5.1 (self-computed); whether that was a routine new version or a response to the entry of Meta (10/12) or Gemini 4 Argon (time-limited $2/$10 on 10/13, secondhand) cannot be told apart from the material available. If it was the latter, the newcomers lowered costs through the incumbent's hands; the diary only says to keep it out of margin assumptions, not that it will not happen, nor that app-layer margins will not improve. "Keeping the top tier in its own subscription" is an inference about intent; compute, data and Wonder's preview label are other explanations.
facts_en: Meta developer blog, 10/12: Wonder costs $4 input and $20 output per million tokens; Full is offered only through Muse Code subscriptions (the $50 and $200 monthly tiers), and Meta says the two perform comparably; the model card calls Full the most capable variant. Anthropic pricing page, 10/12 snapshot: Fable 5.1 at $10/$50, Opus 5.5 at $4/$20. Wonder is not the lowest frontier price: a VentureBeat headline on 10/13 said Google set a time-limited $2/$10 for Gemini 4 Argon (secondhand). Meta's benchmark table (company figures): AA index 58 for Opus 5.5 and 52 for Wonder; DeepSWE 1.1 74.2 for Opus 5.5 and 78.8 for Wonder; of the 14 items in Meta's table (excluding OSWorld binary), Opus 5.5 is higher on 9 and Wonder on 5 (self-computed), and the diary draws no conclusion on which is stronger at the same price. On 11/9 Meta released Ember at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens for up to 200,000 input tokens, the same as Haiku 5.5's starting price, and said the hardest problems go to Wonder; a VentureBeat headline on 11/10 put Ember's estimated per-task cost at about 1/3 of Haiku 5.5 (secondhand). On 11/13 Meta's docs still listed Full as "Not available" on the Model API; Wonder's list price was unchanged and it was still labelled preview.
landing_en: For founders: access to the best model is no moat, so push the cost of switching models as low as it goes. The path most likely to overturn this call is the new small model Zuckerberg described on 10/21: Wonder-level capability delivered more efficiently; if it lands and is cheaper, it is ruled under falsifier (3). The same day he also said Wonder and the stronger models in training can serve high-margin businesses such as the API (a reverse signal, ruled under falsifier (1)), and he expects that in a year a smaller model will deliver Wonder-level intelligence at a fraction of the cost (company claim), which falls outside the falsifier window. For investors: when looking at agent rounds in 2027, keep "one more frontier lab" out of margin assumptions, and move money to apps that switch models without hurting the product or that have proprietary data or a transaction loop.
falsify_en: From 2026-11-13 to 2027-04-12 (all in US Pacific time), 150 days (self-computed). Only two points of the main text are ruled: Meta's top tier stays off the pay-as-you-go API; Meta does not lead a cut in API list prices for Wonder-level capability. ✗ (any one withdraws the main call and the author recants): (1) Muse Wonder Full, or a stronger model that Meta's official materials explicitly rank above muse-wonder-1.0 (Full's successor, or a higher tier then sold only in the Muse Code subscription), gets a public per-token price on the Meta Model API or on any third-party platform Meta officially lists (such as Google Cloud or OpenRouter) and can be called pay-as-you-go; access that requires approval but has a public price also counts; Full or a higher tier switching to usage-based billing only inside Muse Code (not on the Model API or a third-party platform) does not count for (1) and is recorded as a reading, because the app layer still cannot buy it; muse-wonder-1.0 itself and same-tier revisions of it do not count for (1) and are ruled under (2). (2) muse-wonder-1.0 or a direct same-tier successor has its public standard-mode list price on the Meta Model API cut to input ≤ $2.80 or output ≤ $14.00 (per million tokens), at least 30% below the $4/$20 of 2026-11-13 (self-computed); or Meta opens a Contributor mode for the Wonder tier priced at least 30% below the standard price (as of 11/13 Wonder offers no Contributor mode). (3) After 2026-11-13, Meta launches on the Model API any new model or new version of an existing series (such as new Spark or Ember version numbers) that Meta officially calls Wonder-level (as Zuckerberg put it on 10/21, or an equivalent phrase), or whose AA index reading for the same version, as published by Meta, is not lower than muse-wonder-1.0 (52 in the 10/12 table), with a standard-mode public list price of input ≤ $2.80 or output ≤ $14.00 (per million tokens). Not ✗, recorded as readings only: time-limited promotions, batch prices, cache prices; new smaller models below Wonder level (such as Ember on 11/9, which Meta puts at 36 on the AA index, with the hardest problems going to Wonder); private enterprise contracts without a public price; third-party hosting prices for the open-weight Spark Open; following a cut, meaning that within the 30 days before a Meta price cut or the launch of a new model under (3), the standard list price (excluding time-limited prices) of the Anthropic Opus tier, the OpenAI GPT-6 Astra tier or the Google Gemini 4 Argon tier (or their direct successors) fell first to the same level or lower, in which case (2) and (3) do not trigger and the reading is recorded as "following". Verified: by 2027-04-12, neither Meta's docs nor any platform shows a pay-as-you-go price for Wonder Full or the then top tier, and (2) and (3) have not happened. Verified covers only the period to 2027-04-12 and does not mean the main text's 6–18-month call has held; around 2027-10-21 another reading is recorded on the terms of (3). Until then, always ⏳. Risk note: Wonder is still labelled preview, and prices are often changed when a model moves to general availability; the rules above apply all the same.
status_en: ⏳ Open: ENTRY 147 is a retrospective written 2026-11-13 (event date 2026-10-15) and is not scored as a forward call; its falsifier runs from 2026-11-13 to 2027-04-12, and the ledger has no reconciliation or reading yet.

persona: 创始人·AI 安全 / 漏洞发现创业者
q_zh: AI 让找漏洞越来越便宜，安全创业公司还该做漏洞发现吗？钱该挪到哪？
q_en: AI is making bug-finding cheap: should a security startup still build vulnerability discovery, and where should the money go?
lead_zh: 只做「找」的别挤了：找漏洞越来越便宜，引擎在前沿实验室手里，稀缺的是把补丁送进修不动的设备，钱该挪向托管运行时、嵌入式资产清点、固件补丁远程推送（补记，写于 2026-11-13，事件日 10/23）。OpenAI 11/4 自报拿下一个 Linux 提权利用平均约 1,280 美元，补丁一并生成；Wiz 10/27 称一周后其受影响客户约一半没修完。
judgment_zh: 10/21–22 的共识是 AI 挖出波及「70% 网站」（公司称）的漏洞，发现端是新金矿；到 11/13「修补是瓶颈」在安全媒体里也已是共识。日记只在两处分开：钱按「修得到」定价，只做找第三方软件未知漏洞的不投；「70% 网站」的叙事说伤在网站，到 11/13 公开确认得手的两起入口都是安全厂商自家设备。钱这一点分歧较窄：一级市场 2026 年给 AI 攻击型安全公司 20 亿到 25 亿美元以上估值（二手，不点名），其中一家是自主渗透测试，属于日记不劝退的验证端；没找到纯发现端拿到 10 亿美元以上估值的有日期来源。尾注提示双向打折：「引擎在前沿实验室手里」对同在发现端的 Anthropic 定位有利；「硬件安全厂商估值不打折」涉及 Anthropic 的合作方 Palo Alto Networks。
facts_zh: PHP 10/21 修的两枚 RCE（CVSS v4.0 9.2），报告者都用了前沿模型，苗头 2024 年人工审计时已出现；OpenAI 同日称给资源有限的防守方提供 10 亿美元补贴额度（公司称）。OpenAI 11/4：API 费 $1,213,430 拿下 948 个 Linux 提权利用，公司称 $1,279/个、含失败尝试（只算成功约 $359/个），同一流水线生成 948 个补丁；7 月一轮约 $3,095/个，到 10 月降约 59%（均为自算），模型和批次不同，只当方向。Wiz（Google 旗下）10/27：最初受影响的组织里仍易受攻击的不到 53%（客户遥测，公司称；偏乐观，推断）。到 11/13 公开确认得手的两起：Palo Alto Networks 的 PAN-OS 10/23–24 约 25 台被拿到 root（研究方称，二手，量小；Unit 42 确认，称已打补丁的客户不受影响）；Check Point 网关 10/30 起被打，打的是修复发布约一周后仍未打补丁的网关。
landing_zh: 对创业者：别再做只找第三方软件未知漏洞的发现端，补丁生成也别做，OpenAI 的流水线已连补丁一起生成；转做客户环境里的验证暴露面、修补排序和送达，或托管运行时（自动跟版本）、嵌入式资产清点与固件补丁编排、能远程推补丁或虚拟补丁的产品，虚拟补丁配源站隔离。用已知漏洞做自主渗透测试的不在「别挤」之内，但按漏洞或工时计价的渗透测试单价会被压（推断）。对投资人：只做找第三方软件未知漏洞的不投；硬件安全厂商估值不打折，尽调问补丁几天进固件、客户多久装上。
falsify_zh: 起算 2026-11-13，不计入事前命中；观察期到 2027-04-30，终审在 2027-05-15 前后。只裁定正文两件事，两条分开裁定：「只做找未知漏洞的创业公司别去挤」和「确认被打进去的在设备端」。✗①（发现端）：2026-11-13 至 2027-04-30 之间，有一家公司首次公开 ARR 达到或超过 2,500 万美元（以公司公告或监管申报为准），且同时满足：用 AI 发现第三方软件里的未知漏洞是主营；2026 年内在 CVE 致谢里以发现者身份出现过；不隶属前沿实验室或云厂商。第三方软件指既不是该公司自己的、也不是付费客户自研的软件（开源项目和商业厂商产品）；「主营」以这类发现带来的收入，或公司公开自述的主要业务为准。触发即记 ✗，撤回「创业公司别挤发现端」。在客户环境里用已知漏洞做自主渗透测试、验证暴露面的公司不计入，这类已有一家在 2026-10-20 称 ARR 超过 1 亿美元（公司称，二手），发生在起算前，不计。到期仍没有，记「未触发」，不算命中（私营公司不披露 ARR 不等于做不大）；期间记 ⏳。现值：截至 2026-11-13，用 Google 新闻检索没找到符合定义的 ARR 披露。✗②（设备端）：统计 2026-11-13 至 2027-04-30 之间首次公开确认、初始入口是 PHP2Shell（CVE-2026-109618/109619）的入侵活动；经 CVE-2026-115560 的入侵单列记录，不计入下面的 n。按攻击活动计，多份报告说的是同一活动只算一起。「设备」指防火墙、VPN 或远程接入网关、NAS、路由器、工控和楼宇控制器，以及其他出厂内嵌 PHP 的硬件或虚拟设备镜像；受害方在通用服务器上自己部署的网站不算设备。2027-04-30 收口时统计：n ≥ 5 且设备入口占比低于 50%，记 ✗，撤回「确认被打进去的在设备端、钱往设备补丁挪」；n ≥ 5 且不低于 50%，记已验证。
status_zh: ⏳ 进行中：ENTRY 151 为补记，写于 2026-11-13（事件日 2026-10-23），已入台账、不计入事前命中；证伪口两条分开裁定（发现端 ARR 线、设备端入侵占比），设备端 n 不足 5 起记读数不足、不裁定；观察期到 2027-04-30，2027-05-15 前后终审，暂无对账记录。
lead_en: Startups that only do the “finding” should stay out: bug-finding keeps getting cheaper, the engine sits with the frontier labs, and what is scarce is getting patches into devices that are hard to fix, so move the money to managed runtimes, embedded asset inventory and remote firmware patch delivery (retrospective, written 2026-11-13; event date 10/23). OpenAI reported on 11/4 that one Linux privilege-escalation exploit cost about $1,280 on average, with the patch generated alongside; Wiz said on 10/27 that a week on, about half of its affected customers had not finished patching.
judgment_en: The consensus on 10/21–22 was that AI had dug up a bug reaching “70% of websites” (company claim) and that discovery was the new gold mine; by 11/13, “patching is the bottleneck” was also the consensus in the security press. The diary parts ways in only two places: money should be priced on whether the fix can be delivered, so it does not back companies that only find unknown bugs in third-party software; and while the “70% of websites” story put the damage on websites, the two compromises publicly confirmed by 11/13 both entered through security vendors' own devices. On money the disagreement is narrow: private markets in 2026 gave AI offensive-security companies valuations of $2 billion to $2.5 billion and up (secondary sources, unnamed), one of them an autonomous penetration-testing company on the validation side the diary does not warn off; the diary found no dated source of a pure discovery company valued above $1 billion. The endnote asks for discounting in both directions: “the engine sits with the frontier labs” favours the positioning of Anthropic, itself on the discovery side, and “do not discount hardware security vendors' valuations” touches Palo Alto Networks, an Anthropic partner.
facts_en: PHP fixed two RCEs on 10/21 (CVSS v4.0 9.2), and the reporters all used frontier models; early signs had already surfaced in a 2024 manual audit. OpenAI said the same day it was offering $1 billion in subsidised credits to under-resourced defenders (company claim). OpenAI on 11/4: $1,213,430 in API fees yielded 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits, $1,279 each by the company's count including failed attempts (about $359 each counting only successful attempts), and the same pipeline generated 948 patches; a July run cost about $3,095 each, a drop of about 59% by October (both self-computed), with a different model and batch, so read it as direction only. Wiz (part of Google) on 10/27: fewer than 53% of the initially affected organisations were still vulnerable (customer telemetry, company claim; likely optimistic, by inference). The two compromises publicly confirmed by 11/13: Palo Alto Networks' PAN-OS, about 25 devices rooted on 10/23–24 (researchers' count, secondary, a small number; confirmed by Unit 42, which says patched customers were not affected); and Check Point gateways hit from 10/30, gateways that were still unpatched about a week after the fix was released.
landing_en: For founders: stop building pure discovery of unknown bugs in third-party software, and skip patch generation too, since OpenAI's pipeline already generates the patches; move to verifying exposure, ranking fixes and delivering patches inside the customer's environment, or to managed runtimes (tracking versions automatically), embedded asset inventory and firmware patch orchestration, and products that can push patches or virtual patches remotely, with virtual patches paired with origin isolation. Autonomous penetration testing with known bugs is outside the “don't crowd in” call, though per-bug or per-hour pentest pricing is likely to be squeezed (inference). For investors: do not back companies that only find unknown bugs in third-party software; do not discount hardware security vendors' valuations, and in diligence ask how many days a patch takes to reach firmware and how long customers take to install it.
falsify_en: Clock starts 2026-11-13, not scored as a forward call; observation runs to 2027-04-30, with the final ruling around 2027-05-15. Only two claims in the entry are ruled, separately: “startups that only find unknown bugs should not crowd in” and “confirmed break-ins are at the device end”. ✗(1) (discovery end): between 2026-11-13 and 2027-04-30, a company first publicly reports ARR at or above $25 million (company announcement or regulatory filing governs) and also meets all of these: using AI to find unknown bugs in third-party software is its main business; it appeared as the finder in CVE credits during 2026; it is not affiliated with a frontier lab or a cloud provider. Third-party software means software that is neither the company's own nor built in-house by its paying customers (open-source projects and commercial vendors' products); “main business” is judged by revenue from such discoveries or by the company's own public description of its main business. If triggered, mark ✗ and withdraw “startups should not crowd into discovery”. Companies that run autonomous penetration tests with known bugs and verify exposure inside customer environments do not count; one such company already said on 2026-10-20 that its ARR exceeds $100 million (company claim, secondary), which happened before the clock started and does not count. If there is still none at expiry, mark “not triggered”, not a hit (a private company not disclosing ARR does not mean it cannot grow large); ⏳ in the meantime. Current value: as of 2026-11-13, a Google News search found no ARR disclosure meeting the definition. ✗(2) (device end): count the intrusion campaigns first publicly confirmed between 2026-11-13 and 2027-04-30 whose initial entry was PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619); intrusions via CVE-2026-115560 are logged separately and not counted in n below. Counting is by campaign: several reports on the same campaign count as one. A “device” means a firewall, a VPN or remote-access gateway, a NAS, a router, an industrial or building controller, or any other hardware or virtual appliance image that ships with PHP embedded; a website the victim deployed itself on a general-purpose server is not a device. At the 2027-04-30 close: if n ≥ 5 and devices are the initial entry in less than 50% of cases, mark ✗ and withdraw “confirmed break-ins are at the device end, and the money moves to device patching”; if n ≥ 5 and the share is not below 50%, mark verified.
status_en: ⏳ Open: ENTRY 151 is a retrospective, written 2026-11-13 (event date 2026-10-23), on the judgment ledger and not scored as a forward call; its two falsifier tests (a discovery-end ARR line and the device share of confirmed intrusions) are ruled separately, and fewer than 5 device-end cases is an insufficient reading, not ruled; observation runs to 2027-04-30 with the final ruling around 2027-05-15, and there is no reconciliation note yet.

persona: 创始人·向银行、保险卖 agent 的企业级创始人
q_zh: 向银行、保险公司卖 agent，采购尽调现在会多查哪些门槛？
q_en: Selling AI agents to banks and insurers: what new procurement checks should I prepare for?
lead_zh: 日记推断采购会多查两道门（两篇均为补记，写于 2026-11-13）：一查模型内部能否独立审计，开放权重买方自己能审，闭源的要在合同里写监控接口或报告；二查工具够得着哪些机器、能否一人触发转账、权限能否一键收回，买方按热钱包敞口审。后一道的案例是币安被盗案，受影响资产约 63.4 亿美元（公司称）。
judgment_zh: 主流在争 Goodfire「神经元可读」对不对，安全圈对币安案的共识是内部 AI 工具的监控和权限范围没管好；日记的增量只在买方和采购门槛：审计要碰模型内部，谁拿得到权重谁能审；AI 工具够得着的机器，按热钱包的钥匙来管。日记只主张 AI 工具扩大了可达范围，不主张它是必要条件。反面读数：受监管买家眼下接受厂商自出的监控，「采购会查能否独立审计」与这一现状相反，是推断。币安案一侧也有反面读数：大机构可能自建（币安 11/3 称已重建该 AI 工具和访问控制），第三方厂商的机会更可能在中型机构和 agent 卖方。
facts_zh: ENTRY 148：Goodfire 称 10/8 已在中国开放权重模型上跑激活探针监控，成本约为 LLM 逐轮审查的 1/50（公司称）；到 11/13 没有检索到其神经元级结论在非 Qwen 模型族上的独立复现，也没有检索到受监管机构把内部审计列为采购条件。闭源一侧，据 Anthropic S-1，其 9 月宣布的 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards 与 100 多家金融、医疗、公共部门客户共同开发；日记的读法是它看行为与日志、不开放内部状态。ENTRY 155：币安 11/3 报告称，攻击者借一名工程师的电脑和内部 AI 工具拿下另两名钱包工程师的电脑，找到容器部署令牌，10/29（UTC）凭它调用钱包签名服务；工具名称和权限未公开；恶意的 EIP-7702 授权不能立即撤销，要另发交易清除（公司称）。
landing_zh: 对创业者：把能接内部监控列进选型，用闭源模型就在合同里要监控接口或报告；单人不可触发和一键撤销做成默认，备好工具够得着哪些机器、能签什么的权限清单。对投资人：尽调问被投 agent 能签什么、权限能否一键收回；可解释性公司定价先数部署监控合同，只为别家复现过的部分付钱。
falsify_zh: ENTRY 148：起算 2026-11-13（补记，不计入事前命中），终审 2027-07-15，按截至 2027-06-30 的公开材料裁定。②采购标准（检验 P1「采购会查模型内部能否独立审计」）：✗ 条件是 2026-11-13 至 2027-06-30 期间，没有一家受监管的银行、保险公司、医疗机构，也没有金融或医疗监管机构，在官网、监管文件或新闻稿中公开把「模型内部状态（神经元或激活层面）可审计或可监控」列为模型采购、agent 上线或合规条件；已验证：同期至少一家公开列出，且条件写明由买方自己或买方指定的独立第三方执行；只接受厂商自证或厂商出具监控报告的，记「部分成立」，只记读数、不算已验证；只宣布使用某可解释性产品或做研究合作的，不算条件。ENTRY 155：起算 2026-11-13，不计入事前命中。裁定 P1「工具够得着哪些机器、能否一人触发转账，买方会按热钱包敞口审」。✗：2026-11-13 至 2027-04-30 之间，下面两类都没有新出现，作者撤回 P1 这句（起算日现值为零：只算 2026-11-13 之后新发布的）。① 采购问卷：Shared Assessments 在此期间发布的 SIG 新版，或 FS-ISAC 公开发布的第三方风险、供应商尽调材料，新加入的条目须问到 AI 工具或 agent 对签名、支付、生产部署系统或其凭证的可达范围，或能否单人触发签名或资金操作，或权限能否撤销。② 保险：按终审时 NAIC 最新公布的网络险直保保费排名前十的保险集团，或劳合社市场公告，在新公开的保单条款、附加条款、投保问卷或业绩材料里，单列内部 AI 工具或 agent 对支付、签名系统可达范围的核保问题，或为 AI 工具或 agent 发起的资金或资产转移设单独除外或分项限额。裁定：①、② 任一类出现至少一条，记已验证；两类都没有，记 ✗ 并撤回；终审前记 ⏳；终审 2027-05-14，按 Shared Assessments、FS-ISAC、各保险集团官网和劳合社公告的发布日一次性检索；某一类材料拿不到（如 SIG 新版到 2027-04-30 未发布或条目不公开），该类记 source-missing，按另一类裁定；两类都拿不到，整条记 source-missing，不裁定
status_zh: ⏳ 进行中：ENTRY 148、155 均为 2026-11-13 补记，不计入事前命中，台账暂无对账记录。ENTRY 148 终审 2027-07-15，采购标准一条现值 0；ENTRY 155 终审 2027-05-14，起算日现值为零。
lead_en: The diary infers that procurement will add two gates (both from retrospective entries written 2026-11-13): first, whether the model's internal state can be audited independently, which the buyer can do itself with open weights, while with a closed model the contract has to require a monitoring interface or reports; second, which machines the tool can reach, whether one person can trigger a transfer and whether access can be revoked in one step, which the buyer will review as hot-wallet exposure. The case behind the second gate is the Binance theft, with about $6.34 billion of assets impacted (company figure).
judgment_en: The mainstream is arguing over whether Goodfire's claim that neurons are readable is right, and the security community's consensus on the Binance case is that the internal AI tool's monitoring and permissions were poorly controlled; the diary's increment is only on the buyer side and the procurement bar: an audit has to touch model internals, so whoever can reach the weights can audit; machines an AI tool can reach should be managed like hot-wallet keys. The diary claims only that AI tools widened what attackers could reach, not that they were necessary. Contrary reading: regulated buyers currently accept vendor-provided monitoring, so "procurement will check independent auditability" runs against that status quo and is an inference. The Binance side has a contrary reading too: large institutions may build their own (Binance said on 11/3 it had rebuilt the AI tool and its access controls), so the opening for third-party vendors is more likely at mid-sized institutions and agent sellers.
facts_en: ENTRY 148: Goodfire says it was already running activation-probe monitors on Chinese open-weight models on 10/8, at about 1/50 the cost of LLM review of every turn (company claim); as of 11/13 the diary had found no independent replication of its neuron-level result on a non-Qwen model family, and no regulated institution listing internal auditing as a procurement condition. On the closed side, per Anthropic's S-1, Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which it announced in September, was co-developed with more than 100 financial, healthcare and public-sector customers; in the diary's reading it looks at behaviour and logs without opening internal state. ENTRY 155: Binance's 11/3 report says attackers used one engineer's computer and an internal AI tool to take over two other wallet engineers' computers, found a container deployment token, and on 10/29 (UTC) used it to call the wallet signing service; the tool's name and permissions were not disclosed; a malicious EIP-7702 authorization cannot be revoked immediately and needs a separate transaction to clear (company claim).
landing_en: For founders: make the ability to plug in internal monitoring a model-selection criterion, and on a closed model require a monitoring interface or reports in the contract; make no-single-person triggering and one-click revocation the default, and have a permissions list ready showing which machines the tool can reach and what it can sign. For investors: in diligence ask what a portfolio agent can sign and whether its access can be revoked in one step; price interpretability companies on deployment-monitoring contracts first, and pay only for what others have replicated.
falsify_en: ENTRY 148: Starts 2026-11-13 (retrospective, not counted as a prior hit), final ruling 2027-07-15, judged on public material as of 2027-06-30. persona: 创始人·法律 / 金融垂直 AI CEO
q_zh: GDPx 上金融、法律几乎零分，做法律、金融 AI 的创业公司该怎么向投资人讲护城河？
q_en: Frontier models score near zero on GDPx finance and legal tasks: how should a legal or finance AI startup present its moat to investors?
lead_zh: 别把 GDPx 的近零分当护城河证书讲，要讲客户验收单：近零分只是「模型做不到」的公开读数，随新模型刷新，押「模型做不到」的护城河要标到期日，押客户验收单的，模型变强先变成毛利（补记，写于 2026-11-13，事件日 11/4）。做法是把验收标准做成私有评测、写进合同、按验收通过收费，每季度用最新模型重跑，和 GDPx 同领域分数并排给投资人看；11/9 数据里金融二元评分最高仍 2.78%，法律无一通过。
judgment_zh: 主流把 12% 和零分读成 agent 离替代高价值白领还早，市场把金融、法律的近零二元分当垂直 AI 的安全垫（推断）；分数会很快涨是 SemiAnalysis 自己的预期（每 3–6 个月发新版），也算共识。日记的不同在估值读法：近零分是护城河的公开期限读数，估值要挂在这块表上。依据是出题方都是 RL 环境创业公司，生意就是给实验室卖训练任务，实验室为单个高质量任务付 5000 美元以上；各出题方只公开一道样题，实验室够不着考题，但能买到同类任务，所以二元读数会离开地板（推断）。11/9 刷新时综合分 7 天从 12% 升到 16.4%，金融、法律二元分没动，所以不说护城河在加速到期，只说期限从此可读、该被定价。分数若靠买到的同类任务涨上来，未必等于客户真实场景能交付（推断），所以要拿客户私评对照，不单看 GDPx。
facts_zh: SemiAnalysis 11/2 发布 GDPx：206 题、11 个领域，首发综合得分最高 12%；综合得分是 11 个领域等权平均，不能说「做成 12% 的任务」。金融 24 题全部出自同一笔 PE 交易的复刻数据室，法律 20 题覆盖 8 个执业领域，量的是交易型金融与公司法务交付，不代表全部法律、金融 AI 场景。11/9 数据：金融二元最高 2.78%（72 次尝试过 2 次，自算），法律 21 个模型全为 0；金融部分分最高 54.59%，同一模型金融二元为 0；法律部分分最高 38.44%。题量小，金融一次通过约 +1.39 个点（自算），一两次侥幸就能让读数跳动。
landing_zh: 对创业者：领投方会要求拆开两类收入（推断），先自己拆：靠「通用模型做不到」挣的那部分标到期日，按通过验收的交付收的那部分按毛利讲；光有私评还不够，要写进合同和定价。模型厂自己也在卖法律、金融行业产品（Anthropic S-1/A 11/10；OpenAI 9/10 推出 ChatGPT for Financial Services，VentureBeat 标题），按结果收费的公司同样会被压价，「模型变强先变成毛利」只在验收标准与合同留在公司手里时成立（推断）。对投资人：靠「模型做不到」挣的收入按有限期限折现，这是新一轮定价时的做法；尽调时可要求公司用最新前沿模型跑自家私评、每季度更新，和 GDPx 同领域读数并排看。
falsify_zh: 起算 2026-11-13（补记，不计入事前命中），只裁定正文这一句：「金融、法律的二元读数会离开地板」。裁定量：gdpx.semianalysis.com 排行榜 v1 题集（206 题、11 个领域），Metric 用默认的 Score（各任务预定的评分法，金融、法律两域即二元评分），取金融（24 题）与法律（20 题）两域所有上榜模型的最高分，同时记下当时数据文件的 updatedAt。裁定量固定为二元分：若站点默认 Score 对金融、法律改显示部分分，改用数据文件的二元 score 字段或站点二元口径；取不到二元分记源缺失，任何时候不用部分分裁定。✗：到 2027-05-13，金融最高分仍 ≤2.78%，且法律仍为 0%，作者改口，承认 6 个月内这块表没走到金融、法律，「通用模型做不到」这段窗口比本篇设想的长，垂直 AI 不必按这块表折现；✗ 线等于现值，不高于现值。✗ 只在到期前 v1 至少给 1 个 2026-11-13 之后发布的前沿模型打过分时成立（前沿模型指 Anthropic、OpenAI、Google、Meta、xAI 任一家在 2026-11-13 后发布的当期旗舰）；一个都没有，记「裁定源缺失（无新模型）」，不裁定、不改口。已验证：2027-05-13 前任一时点，v1 题集里金融或法律任一域最高分 ≥10%（按颗粒度自算：金融一次通过约 +1.39 个点，需 ≥8/72 次；法律一次约 +1.67 个点，需 ≥6/60 次）。⏳：两线之间记 ⏳，只记读数；到期仍在两线之间，记「未到线」，不计命中，也不改口；只有任一域最高分 ≥5%（金融 ≥4/72 次、法律 ≥3/60 次，自算），才可加注「方向对」。换版：SemiAnalysis 称每 3–6 个月发新版；新版仍公布 v1 题集分数的，按 v1 裁定；v1 题集在 2027-02-13 前停更（之后不再给新模型打 v1 分）、只剩换题新版的，记「裁定源缺失（换版）」，不裁定、不改口；v1 在 2027-02-13 之后停更的，按 v1 最后一版数据裁定。
status_zh: ⏳ 进行中。ENTRY 157 为 2026-11-13 补记（事件日 2026-11-04），不计入事前命中；证伪口自 2026-11-13 起算，终审在 2027-05-13 后一周内。截至 2026-11-13，✗ 与已验证两头都还没有被事实决定。
lead_en: Do not pitch GDPx's near-zero scores as a moat certificate; pitch the client's acceptance sheet: the near-zero scores are only a public reading of what models still cannot do, refreshed with every new model, so a moat that bets on models being unable to do the work needs an expiry date, while for a moat that bets on the client's acceptance sheet, stronger models turn into gross margin first (retrospective, written 2026-11-13; event date 11/4). In practice: turn the acceptance criteria into a private evaluation, write it into contracts, charge per delivery that passes acceptance, rerun it with the latest model every quarter and show it to investors next to the GDPx score for your domain; in the 11/9 data the best binary score in finance was still 2.78%, and no model passed a single legal task.
judgment_en: The mainstream read the 12% and the zeros as a sign that agents are still far from replacing high-value white-collar work, and the market treats the near-zero binary scores in finance and legal as a safety cushion for vertical AI (an inference); that scores will rise quickly is SemiAnalysis's own expectation (a new version every 3–6 months), and counts as consensus too. Where the diary differs is the valuation reading: the near-zero scores are a public expiry reading on the moat, and valuations should be pegged to this board. The basis: the task writers are all RL-environment startups whose business is selling training tasks to labs, and labs pay $5,000 or more for a single high-quality task; each task writer publishes only one sample task, so labs cannot reach the test itself but can buy similar tasks, and the binary readings will therefore leave the floor (an inference). In the 11/9 refresh the overall score rose from 12% to 16.4% in 7 days while the finance and legal binary scores did not move, so the diary does not say the moat is expiring faster, only that its term is now readable and should be priced. If scores rise on purchased tasks of the same kind, that does not necessarily mean delivery in real client scenarios (an inference), which is why the check is the client's private evaluation, not GDPx alone.
facts_en: SemiAnalysis released GDPx on 11/2: 206 tasks across 11 domains, and the top overall score at launch was 12%; the overall score is an equal-weighted average of the 11 domains, so it cannot be read as "completing 12% of tasks". All 24 finance tasks come from a replica data room of a single PE deal, and the 20 legal tasks cover 8 practice areas: it reads transactional finance and corporate legal delivery, not every legal or finance AI use case. 11/9 data: the best binary score in finance is 2.78% (2 passes in 72 attempts, self-computed), and all 21 models score 0 in legal; the best partial score in finance is 54.59%, from a model whose binary finance score is 0; the best partial score in legal is 38.44%. The task count is small: one pass in finance adds about 1.39 points (self-computed), so one or two lucky passes can make the reading jump.
landing_en: For founders: lead investors will ask for the two kinds of revenue to be split (an inference), so split them yourself: put an expiry date on the part earned because general models cannot do the work, and present the part charged per delivery that passes acceptance on gross margin; a private evaluation alone is not enough, it has to be written into contracts and pricing. Model makers sell legal and finance industry products themselves (Anthropic's S-1/A of 11/10; OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Financial Services on 9/10, per a VentureBeat headline), so companies that charge on results will face price pressure too, and "stronger models turn into gross margin first" holds only while the acceptance criteria and the contracts stay with the company (an inference). For investors: discount revenue that depends on models being unable to do the work over a finite term, which is how to price a new round; in diligence you may ask the company to run its own private evaluation with the latest frontier model, updated every quarter, next to the GDPx reading for the same domain.
falsify_en: Counted from 2026-11-13 (a retrospective, not counted as a prior hit), ruling only on this one sentence of the entry: "the binary readings in finance and legal will leave the floor". Measure: the gdpx.semianalysis.com leaderboard v1 task set (206 tasks, 11 domains), with Metric on the default Score (each task's predefined scoring method, which in the finance and legal domains is binary scoring), taking the highest score among all listed models in the finance (24 tasks) and legal (20 tasks) domains and recording the updatedAt of the data file at that time. The measure is fixed to the binary score: if the site's default Score switches to showing partial scores for finance and legal, use the binary score field in the data file or the site's binary metric instead; if no binary score can be obtained, record the source as missing; partial scores are never used for the ruling. ✗: if by 2027-05-13 the best finance score is still ≤2.78% and legal is still 0%, the author recants, admitting that within 6 months this board did not reach finance and legal, that the window in which general models cannot do the work is longer than this entry assumed, and that vertical AI need not be discounted against this board; the ✗ line equals the current value and is not above it. ✗ holds only if, before expiry, v1 has scored at least 1 frontier model released after 2026-11-13 (a frontier model means the then-current flagship released after 2026-11-13 by any of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta or xAI); if there is none, record "ruling source missing (no new model)", with no ruling and no recanting. Verified: at any point before 2027-05-13, the best score in either the finance or the legal domain of the v1 task set is ≥10% (self-computed from the granularity: one pass in finance adds about 1.39 points, requiring ≥8/72 attempts; one pass in legal adds about 1.67 points, requiring ≥6/60). ⏳: between the two lines, record ⏳ and log readings only; if still between the lines at expiry, record "line not reached", counted neither as a hit nor as a recant; only if either domain's best score reaches ≥5% (finance ≥4/72, legal ≥3/60, self-computed) may the note "direction right" be added. Version change: SemiAnalysis says it releases a new version every 3–6 months; if a new version still publishes v1 task-set scores, rule on v1; if the v1 task set stops being updated before 2027-02-13 (no new model receives a v1 score after that) and only a new version with different tasks remains, record "ruling source missing (version change)", with no ruling and no recanting; if v1 stops being updated after 2027-02-13, rule on the last v1 data.
status_en: ⏳ Open. ENTRY 157 is a retrospective written 2026-11-13 (event date 2026-11-04) and is not counted as a prior hit; the falsifier counts from 2026-11-13, with the final ruling within one week after 2027-05-13. As of 2026-11-13, neither the ✗ side nor the verified side had been decided by events.
